title: Education and Other Legislation Amendment (Abolishing Indexation and Raising the Minimum Repayment Income for Education and Training Loans) Bill 2022
short_title: Education and Other Legislation Amendment (Abolishing Indexation and Raising the Minimum Repayment Income for Education and Training Loans) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would end indexation of specified education and training loans and raise the income level at which borrowers must start making compulsory repayments.
Indexation would be removed from the financial year starting 1 July 2022, with a median-wage repayment threshold applying from the 2023-24 income year.
The changes would cover higher education, vocational education, trade support and specified student assistance loans, including student start-up and financial supplement debts.
changes: The minimum repayment income would be defined by reference to median earnings rather than the existing threshold.
Annual median wages would be calculated using 52 times the published weekly earnings figure.
The minister could determine an earnings figure if required statistics were delayed, with reasons explaining the calculation.
summary.affected: People with higher education, vocational training, trade support and specified student assistance loan debts would be affected.
